about: Which pursuits each of a person's records belongs to, as DATA the one scope owner reads (src/record-scope.mjs). The links it follows are the links records already carry: every `links` row of src/record-sharing.json (a decision's cited_pursuits), plus the `links` rows here, plus the person's own choices (a record-scope record). A link { from, field, to } says a record of stored type `from` names records of kind `to` in `field` (an id, a list of ids, or an object keyed by ids). A link with `each` reads a list of objects instead, each naming its own kind at `each.kind` and its id at `each.id` (a message's about). `refs` turns an id named with a kind into the id the rest of Trillion knows that record by (a file named by its identity is `file:<identity>`, a tool by its id is `tool:<tool id>`, as src/record-sharing.mjs names them). A link `kept_by` "model" is kept by the record store itself as participation under its `role` (src/record-model.json declares it among the kind's parts), a key of the store's pages, so it costs no scope_links row (one row and two index entries for each record named): read back through the store's holdersOf where the index is read. `stored_prefixes` name the kind of a record that is not kept as an EEAF record, by the start of its id. `dimensions` are what a record is scoped by, each with the query `param` that names its chosen values: `through_links` true means reached through any chain of links (a message about a decision that cites a pursuit is in that pursuit, and a pursuit scoped under another pursuit is inside it). `values_from` names where the dimension's values are read: `pursuits` (the person's own pursuits, src/pursuit-rooms.mjs). `room` is where a value's people and shared things are, the same thing (src/pursuit-rooms.mjs): `field` names the room on the value, so what is in a chosen pursuit's room, or in the rooms of the pursuits inside it, is in that pursuit too: links naming the room (`target_kind`), the copies of the person's records the Network holds there (src/record-offers.mjs ownCopiesIn) and the things its members put there; `param` is the earlier parameter that named rooms directly, still read, each room standing for its pursuit. `kinds` are the kinds of record a screen or an AI asks for, each covering the stored types listed; `space_kind` and `space_origin` project Space-made items through a fresh membership-checked Network read without private copies; `space_items` true covers all things members added to the chosen pursuits' rooms. `lists` are the workspace list answers that take a `scope` parameter, which the workspace sends on every read of them while the person's Focus is set (src/workspace/api.ts narrowListsBy); a list of capabilities everyone uses whatever they focus on (the Workshop's tools) is not one of them: `path` is the address, a segment { param } matching any one segment under that name; each `rows` entry says where the rows are (`at`), how a row names its record (`ref`: `path` inside the row, `or_path` when the first is absent, a `prefix`, or `prefix_by` a field of the row), and `in_space` the room a row is in: `param`, every row is in the room named by the address, or `path` inside the row (a calendar's meeting names its own room). A row in the room of a chosen pursuit is in that pursuit. `values` are the words and icons a filter shows for each dimension. `refused` are the words said when a request cannot be answered.

naming.about: How a record that names another reads in that record's trace (trace_item's records, a decision page's What came after). `title`: per stored type, the places its words may be, the first one found wins; a type with no row reads as its kind. `at`: the places a record keeps when it was made, the first one found wins.

refused.not_your_pursuit: is not one of your pursuits.
refused.inside_itself: is this pursuit or a pursuit set under it, so it cannot also hold it: choose a pursuit outside it.
refused.merge_into_inside: is set under the pursuit being joined into it, so it cannot take that pursuit's place: move it out from under that pursuit first, or join them the other way round.
refused.private_reach: This sign-in reaches only some of your pursuits, so it cannot read or change which pursuits your private records belong to.
refused.unknown_kind: is not a kind of record Trillion lists. The kinds are:
refused.bad_scope: scope is a JSON object like {"pursuits": ["pursuit:launch"]}, or {"saved": "<screen id>"} for the scope you saved.
